title: Transient headroom allocator and invoice protection policy
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define and implement a transient headroom allocator (temporary boosts / surge credits) for Dedicated customers, plus an invoice protection policy that amortizes short-lived overages and provides clear owner-level visibility. This ticket covers the allocator algorithm, autoscaling interactions, credit accounting model for billing, telemetry hooks, and an operator UI to inspect and revoke BOOST leases.
acceptance_criteria: Allocator issues temporary boosts (leases) when capacity pool signals indicate short latency spikes without consuming reserved capacity long-term
Boost leases expire automatically after TTL and are visible in the console with reason and owner metadata
Overage billing for transient boosts is amortized: invoices include a smoothing line item and a one-time notification explaining protected credits
No change to SLO calculations for customers with active reserved capacity; bursts should not penalize baseline SLOs unless sustained beyond amortization window
End-to-end tests that simulate surges validate that boosts allocate, KV cache and batching remain functional, and billing records match amortization rules
implementation_plan: Design: finalize lease semantics (TTL, renewal policy, max concurrent boosts per customer)
Runtime: implement headroom allocator service in runtime controller with token-rate estimator and short-window smoothing
Autoscaler integration: allocator signals to autoscaler to prefer pre-warmed spare lanes; fallbacks trigger when sustained
Billing: add surge_credit ledger entries and invoice amortizer that spreads cost of boosts over N billing cycles or consumes pre-purchased credits
Console: add Boosts table and detail flyout showing TTL, trigger reason, and linked traces
Testing: unit tests, integration test harness with SyntheticTrafficRunner, and chaos test to ensure graceful revocation
rollout_steps: Run in canary for <10 customers for 2 weeks and collect telemetry
Open beta for customers on Dedicated with opt-in consent; monitor cost reconciliation closely
Gradually expand removal of opt-in depending on stability and billing reconciliation results
GA with docs, SDK flags, and tenant-visible audit logs
decision_log: 2026-01-30: Chose TTL=10m default with exponential backoff for renewal after engineering review to limit long-term exposure
2026-02-03: Amortization window set to single-billing-cycle by default; PM requested option to spread over 3 cycles later
2026-02-06: Opted to treat boosts as metered add-on rather than free credits to avoid hidden cost shift; introduced invoice-protection threshold for small, infrequent bursts
tradeoffs: Short TTL reduces billing exposure but increases churn in allocator decisions; risk of frequent renewable boosts increasing complexity
Smoothing costs across cycles reduces immediate sticker shock but can delay cost attribution for customers and finance reconciliation
Making boosts free for low-frequency events increases customer goodwill but shifts costs to other customers or Redwood unless covered by 'surge premium' pricing
outstanding_risks: Customers with automated budget rules may still hit hard caps when boosts are issued — need clear console signals and webhooks
Invoice amortization could create mismatches in Revenue recognition if finance isn't aligned;
Edge-case where allocator renewals plus autoscaler race causes double-provisioning of GPUs for short windows
qa_plan: Create SyntheticTrafficRunner scenarios: short spike (2m), medium spike (12m), sustained spike (2h)
Verify billing ledger entries: surge_credit.created, surge_credit.consumed, amortized.entry per tenant
Perform load tests on allocator at 10k tenant events/hour to validate performance
Manual review of console Boosts UI for canary tenants
